title: A Spire for the Sigil
premise: Isandro Galloway, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that has gone silent, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When the border wards collapse on the same night every star goes dark, she learns the king of Cael Saren is no longer a man but a vessel for the Sigil, an old power that eats oaths and wears crowns. Hunted by her own guild for knowing too much and sheltered by a found family of smugglers, defrocked priests, and one very stubborn cartographer, Isandro must trace the god's silence to its source and unbind the king before the Sigil finishes rewriting the world's promises. In the end she breaks her own oath to save him, discovering that a silent god was never absent—only listening—and that love freely chosen outlasts any vow written in blood.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a cluttered study in a coastal town, where she collects broken clocks and insists they are all still keeping time somewhere.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A quiet night at the Vellum Guild: she audits entries for bottled storms and borrowed years, trading dry wit with her mentor Corvane while hiding the ache of her god's five-year silence. Emotional beat: comfortable routine masking a hollowed-out faith.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The border wards shatter and every star vanishes in a single breath; guild clients panic, and Isandro feels her oath-mark burn cold for the first time. She finds a ledger page she never wrote, describing tonight. Emotional beat: dread—the world's rules have visibly broken.

chapters.title: A King Wearing Something Else
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with a brief interlude from the court scribe Tam. Summoned to the capital to appraise the crown jewels, Isandro touches the royal sigil and glimpses the thing inside King Aldric—patient, hungry, wearing his memories like a coat. Emotional beat: horror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Guild Does to Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Guild's ruling conclave orders Isandro silenced; Corvane, torn between loyalty and doctrine, burns her file instead of her. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice, and the first hint the Guild serves the Sigil knowingly.

chapters.title: Runaways on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Fleeing the capital, she falls in with a smuggling crew: brash captain Ovesa, ex-priest Brannoc, and cartographer Wren, who maps roads that move. Emotional beat: wary alliance—strangers becoming something like shelter.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Maps What Isn't There
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals her maps chart the Sigil's influence as stains across the land, all converging on the capital—and on Isandro's oath-mark. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared secrets; Isandro realizes she is a key, not just a witness.

chapters.title: Oaths Are Currency
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. At a black-market shrine, Brannoc explains how the Sigil devours sworn vows, which is why the god went silent: it ate the prayers. Isandro tests her broken connection and hears one word—run. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Guild Comes Collecting
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Guild enforcers ambush the crew at a river crossing; Ovesa's improvisation and Isandro's ledger-craft turn the trap around, but a friend dies holding the line. Emotional beat: first real loss; found family sealed in blood.

chapters.title: Letters to a Silent God
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, quiet chapter. Around a fire, she reads aloud the unsent letters she wrote during the god's silence; Wren answers with her own confession of exile. Emotional beat: tenderness—the slow, unspoken love between them takes root.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Ovesa's POV. The crew reaches a trade city where the Sigil's influence has erased residents' names and histories; documents go blank overnight. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness—the stakes become personal and civic, not just royal.

chapters.title: Tam's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The court scribe defects, bringing proof that the king signed away his name willingly to end a famine—desperate bargain, monstrous price. Emotional beat: moral complexity; the enemy was once a good man's hope.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Archive of Vows
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Beneath the capital lies the Archive where every oath ever sworn is stored; the crew infiltrates it to find the original contract binding Aldric. Emotional beat: heist tension laced with awe at the machinery of promise.

chapters.title: The Contract in the King's Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They find the contract—but it requires the sworn party's willing consent to dissolve, meaning Aldric must choose to be unbound. Worse, Corvane arrives, not to stop them but to beg Isandro to stop. Emotional beat: heartbreak at a mentor's surrender.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Using her guild credentials, Isandro gains audience with Aldric and speaks to the man beneath; for three seconds, he surfaces and whispers his daughter's name. Emotional beat: compassion—the king is a prisoner begging through glass.

chapters.title: The Princess Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Princess Sefeya's POV. The Sigil has edited the princess's memories, but a lullaby her father sang survives; she joins the crew, carrying the emotional leverage that might reach him. Emotional beat: fragile hope carried by a child's stubborn love.

chapters.title: Where the God Went Silent
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Following the stain-maps to a drowned temple, the crew finds the god—not dead but swallowed, held inside the Sigil as collateral. To free it, someone must offer an oath the Sigil cannot digest. Emotional beat: terrible clarity about the price.

chapters.title: An Oath the Sigil Cannot Digest
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The answer is a vow given freely with no condition, no reward—an oath of pure gift. Isandro realizes her love for Wren is exactly that. Emotional beat: terror and certainty braided together; she decides without telling anyone.

chapters.title: The Coronation of the Thing
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. On the solstice, the Sigil plans a public coronation-rite to bind the whole nation's oaths at once. The crew scatters to sabotage wards, gates, and choir-lines as the starless sky begins to press down like a lid. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, everything staked.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the throne room, Sefeya's lullaby cracks the Sigil's hold long enough for Aldric to consent; Isandro speaks her freely-given vow, and the contract burns. The god floods back into the world; the Sigil, starving, unravels. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, release, blinding grace.

chapters.title: What Love Costs the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Isandro lies spent, her oath-mark scarred white; the god answers her not with commands but with a question: what will you do now that nothing is owed? Wren holds her hand through the long night. Emotional beat: aftermath, exhaustion, quiet joy.

chapters.title: A New Entry in the Book
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The king, restored and diminished, begins honest reparations; the Guild fractures, and Corvane offers Isandro leadership. She declines, writing instead a new kind of ledger entry—one that records gifts, not debts. Emotional beat: justice rebuilt outside the law.

chapters.title: Stars, Returning
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, mostly Isandro's POV. One year later, aboard Ovesa's ship with Wren, Brannoc, Tam, and Sefeya, Isandro watches the stars come back one by one over open water. Her god says nothing, and for once silence feels like company. Emotional beat: resolution—found family under a mended sky.
